Build a linear ramp temperature trajectory

Source: R/discrete-time-hazard-brms.R
ramp_path.Rd

A convenience function for the path argument of build_hazard_data, useful when there is no logged temperature series: when temperature follows a controlled linear ramp, temp(t) = T_start + rate * t, the nominal ramp stands in for a logged trace. It is vectorised over its arguments: give several ramps at once and it stacks them into one table keyed by path_id.

Usage

ramp_path(path_id, T_start, rate, t_max, by = NULL)

Arguments

path_id, T_start, rate, t_max

The ramp specification, one value per ramp: path_id the identifier, T_start the start temperature, rate in degrees per time unit, and t_max the duration. The four are recycled together, so equal-length vectors describe several ramps and a length-one argument is reused across all of them.

by

An optional numeric giving the sampling step in time. When NULL (the default) the path is just its two endpoints, which the linear interpolation in build_hazard_data reproduces exactly. A value such as by = 5 creates a row every by time units, which then serves as the check schedule in interval mode or a ready-made integration grid in continuous mode.

Value

A data frame with path_id, time and temp, ready to pass to build_hazard_data as its path.

Examples

# One ramp: 20 -> 35 degrees over 60 minutes, as a two-point path.
ramp_path("A", T_start = 20, rate = 0.25, t_max = 60)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   path_id  time  temp
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 A           0    20
#> 2 A          60    35

# Two ramps at different rates, each sampled every 10 minutes (T_start recycled).
ramp_path(c("slow", "fast"), T_start = 20, rate = c(0.2, 0.4),
          t_max = c(75, 40), by = 10)
#> # A tibble: 14 × 3
#>    path_id  time  temp
#>    <chr>   <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 slow        0    20
#>  2 slow       10    22
#>  3 slow       20    24
#>  4 slow       30    26
#>  5 slow       40    28
#>  6 slow       50    30
#>  7 slow       60    32
#>  8 slow       70    34
#>  9 slow       75    35
#> 10 fast        0    20
#> 11 fast       10    24
#> 12 fast       20    28
#> 13 fast       30    32
#> 14 fast       40    36
